newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German states report September CPI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German states report September CPI.

text.p: Following are comments from economists to September consumer price data from the German states of North Rhine-Westphalia and Baden-Wuerttemberg that were released on Tuesday.

Consumer prices in North Rhine-Westphalia fell 0.1 percent month-on-month and rose 1.6 percent over year-ago levels, while prices in Baden-Wuerttemberg fell 0.2 percent month-on-month and rose 1.2 percent year-on-year.
The two are the first of four states to release data that is used to compute preliminary west German inflation data. The west German figure is due to be released Thursday or Friday.
Armin Kayser, Swiss Bank Corp, Frankfurt:

"They look pretty favourable but the fact is that the numbers have benefitted for a strong seasonal effect, which was 0.2 percent in August and 0.3 percent in September. CPI is bottoming out and the current number could be 1.3 percent or 1.4 percent. It is more or less in a sideways movement. CPI is currently bottoming out with no risk of acceleration but only a gradual upturn."
Uwe Angenendt, economist at Berliner Handels und Frankfurter Bank:

"This was in line with our expectations. The figures show a slight worsening which is mainly due to an increase in heating oil prices. In Baden Wuerttemberg these rose 17.7 percent. I would see this as a temporary development and I do not think we will see any acceleration of inflation in the months to come. I see (year on year) inflation at around 1.5 percent by year-end."
